{{nihongo|'''Yana Shrine'''|山那神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

=== Overview ===
The date of foundation is unknown. However, from a ridge tag stating that the shrine building was repaired during the {{ill|Shōryaku|de|Shōryaku|fa|شوریاکو|fr|Ère Shōryaku|ia|Shoryaku|id|Shōryaku|ja|正暦|ko|쇼랴쿠|ru|Сёряку|simple|Shōryaku|sr|Шорјаку|tr|Shōryaku|uk|Сьоряку|zh|正曆 (日本)|zh_yue|正曆 (日本)|qid=Q1324858}} era, it is known to be very old.

In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} it was called Tenjin-sha. In the {{ill|Bunka|Q1373146|qid=Q1373146|lt=Bunka years}}, by judgment of the {{ill|Owari Domain|de|Owari (Han)|fa|قلمرو اوواری|fr|Domaine d'Owari|ja|尾張藩|ko|오와리번|ru|Овари (княжество)|th|แคว้นศักดินาโอวาริ|zh|尾張藩|qid=Q1062072}}, the Tenjin-sha of Minamiyana was identified as the shikinaisha Yana Shrine.

In {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}（{{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 6）, it became a gōsha under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}; === Origins ===
In the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha list}}'', among 22 seats of Niwa District appears "Yana Shrine." In ''Owari-shi'' it says, "Located at Minamiyana and called Tenjin-sha. In the Engishiki Jinmyō list it is Yana Shrine of Niwa District; in Honkoku-chō it appears as Minamiyana Tenjin of Junior Third Rank in the same district."

''Owari Chimeikō'' says, "After Yana village was divided into south and north, the shrine was attached to Minamiyana." ''Owari Shinmeichō Shūsetsu Nara Teikō'' says, "There were two Yana shrines; in the Bunka era, the shrine family Sawaki of Hachiman (south) and shrine family Ozeki of Tenjin (north) contested, and Sawaki won by virtue of hereditary shrine-office service." The same work, citing ''Kanbun Sonson Oboegaki,'' records that among the three Minamiyana shrines (Daimyōjin, Hachiman, Tenjin), "Ōdate Takakado states that this should be Hachimangū of Minamiyana village."

In Fusō there are two shrines with the same name, Yana Shrine, in Minamiyana and {{ill|Yamana, Fuso|Q106705806|qid=Q106705806}}. In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, both used the name Tenjin-sha and each claimed to be the shikinaisha Yana Shrine. By judgment of the {{ill|Owari Domain|de|Owari (Han)|fa|قلمرو اوواری|fr|Domaine d'Owari|ja|尾張藩|ko|오와리번|ru|Овари (княжество)|th|แคว้นศักดินาโอวาริ|zh|尾張藩|qid=Q1062072}}, Minamiyana's Tenjin-sha was designated the shikinaisha Yana Shrine. This area was prone to floods of the {{ill|Kiso River|Q779607|qid=Q779607}}, and because the former Yana Shrine suffered damage and also fell into ruin during the {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}}, its location became unclear. Another theory says that when {{ill|Yamana|ja|山名村|ko|야마나촌 (아이치현)|qid=Q21655059}} split into north and south villages, Yana Shrine was divided into two.

=== Merged shrines ===
* Hachiman Shrine（Takatsuka Hachiman Shrine）- formerly at Hongō lot 81; merged in 1910（Meiji 43）. One theory says it was called Tawada Hachiman and was founded by enshrinement from Tawada Shichiuemon Tameuji in April 1301（Shōan 3）.

=== Zelkova ===
[[File:山那神社のケヤキ.png|thumb|Zelkova tree of Yana Shrine]]
In the precincts stands a giant {{ill|Zelkova serrata|ar|زلكوفا منشارية|arz|زلكوفا منشاريه|az|Zelkova serrata|ceb|Zelkova serrata|cs|Zelkova pilovitá|da|Japansk zelkova|de|Japanische Zelkove|es|Zelkova serrata|eu|Japoniar zelkoba|fa|نارون ژاپنی|fi|Idänselkova|fr|Zelkova serrata|frr|Zelkova serrata|hu|Japán gyertyánszil|id|Terbas jepang|ja|ケヤキ|ko|느티나무|lt|Japoninis skirpstulas|nl|Japanse zelkova|no|Keaki|pl|Brzostownica japońska|pt|Zelkova serrata|pwn|tjeves|ru|Дзельква пильчатая|sco|Zelkova serrata|sv|Zelkova serrata|tr|Zelkova serrata|vi|Zelkova serrata|war|Zelkova serrata|zh|榉树|zh_yue|櫸樹|qid=Q920344}} that seems to tell the shrine's long history; it is designated a Fusō Town cultural property. Height 30 m, root circumference 4.9 m, trunk circumference 4 m, six east-west branches of 8-9 m, and six north-south branches of 5-6 m. This tree is very old and culturally valuable, and has been designated a {{ill|Natural monument|Q23790|qid=Q23790}}.

=== Stage ===
From the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, the {{ill|Owari Domain|de|Owari (Han)|fa|قلمرو اوواری|fr|Domaine d'Owari|ja|尾張藩|ko|오와리번|ru|Овари (княжество)|th|แคว้นศักดินาโอวาริ|zh|尾張藩|qid=Q1062072}} had flourishing {{ill|Stage (theatre)|ar|خشبة مسرح|bew|Panggung (lènong)|bg|Сцена|bxr|Тайзан|ca|Escena|cs|Jeviště|da|Scene (sted)|de|Bühne (Theater)|el|Σκηνή (θέατρο)|eo|Scenejo|es|Escenario|et|Lava|fa|صحنه (تئاتر)|fi|Estradi|fr|Scène (théâtre)|hr|Pozornica|ht|Sèn|hu|Színpad|hy|Բեմ|io|Ceneyo|is|Leiksvið|it|Palcoscenico|ja|舞台|kk|Сахна|ko|무대|lt|Scena|mk|Сцена (театар)|nl|Toneel (vloer)|nn|Scene|no|Scene|pa|ਸਟੇਜ (ਥੀਏਟਰ)|pl|Scena|pt|Palco|ro|Scenă|ru|Сцена|scn|Chiazzata|sd|منچ|sh|Pozornica|simple|Stage (theatre)|sk|Javisko|sl|Oder (gledališče)|sr|Позорница|sv|Scen (anläggning)|tr|Sahne|uk|Сцена|uz|Sahna|zh|舞台|zh_yue|舞台|qid=Q194428}}, and plays were often performed in shrine "kaguradō" halls. In {{ill|Minamiyana Village|Q132044475|qid=Q132044475}}, they became so enthusiastic that they built a full "stage" equipped with a {{ill|Revolving stage|Q253227|qid=Q253227}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=dressing room}}. A major reason was the presence of actor-manager {{ill|Komuro Nakatarō|Q124483423|qid=Q124483423}}, a native of Hongō in the same village, who toured across Tōkai and passionately trained local youth in {{ill|Kabuki|Q199701|qid=Q199701}}. After his death, performances declined, the stage gradually became a martial-arts training hall for youth groups, and in 1939, after a final local performance, it was requisitioned as a supply warehouse by the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army|Q276535|qid=Q276535|lt=Army}}. After the war, welcome entertainment for demobilized soldiers and bought-in plays were held, but the old stage culture did not revive. The building came to be used mainly as a meeting hall and farm-produce collection site; the revolving stage was buried, an entrance was built for easier use as a {{ill|Kominkan|Q8194637|qid=Q8194637}}, and the dressing room was removed, making it smaller. Later, with functional community halls built elsewhere, the building survived again as a warehouse but became deteriorated. Preservation was petitioned as cultural heritage "stage," but since renovation had left it no longer recognizable as a true stage, certification was deemed impossible. After repeated discussion, it was demolished. In October 2013（Heisei 25）, a commemorative monument to the stage was erected.
